paper_title: New ALPS Results on Hidden-Sector Lightweights
notes: ALPS-I (2010) light-shining-through-wall experiment at DESY with a 5 T, HERA dipole (l=4.3 m per side, omega=2.33 eV, ~1.2 kW circulating power). Paper reports 95% C.L. limits on the LSW probability in Table 1 (e.g. 2.25e-25 for magnet on, parallel polarization, vacuum) and presents exclusion plots (Fig. 4) for g_-/g_+ vs m_phi without tabulated coupling values. The data_points above are the pseudoscalar g_- limit reconstructed from the tabulated probability limit via Eq. (5): g = sqrt(P_LSW)^(1/2)... specifically g = P_single^(1/2) * m^2 / (2*omega*B*sin(m^2*l/(4*omega))) with P_single = sqrt(2.25e-25); low-mass plateau g ~ 6.5e-8 GeV^-1, consistent with the published Fig. 4 (axis range 1e-7 to 1e-6 GeV^-1, masses 1e-4 to ~1e-3 eV). Gap near m~1.16e-3 eV is covered by Argon gas runs at a weaker probability limit (10.8e-25). Paper also sets limits on hidden-photon kinetic mixing (Fig. 5) and minicharged particles (Fig. 6); pseudoscalar ALP-photon chosen as the primary/most cited result per the pre-analysis hint.
